answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut mandate creates pressure that favors the proven low-cost vendor switch (memory_c2 achieved sharp unit cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing). However, at 94% assembly line capacity with no buffer and a 14-day renewal deadline, switching primary supply carries delivery risk. Verifying memory_c2 confirms the low-cost vendor's execution track record; verifying memory_c6 establishes the cost-benefit of multi-year commitments. The incumbent's longer-term pricing (memory_c6) plus renegotiation leverage (memory_c4) could also yield 18% cuts, but the timeline is too tight for negotiation cycles. A standard experiment scale—committing to the proven low-cost vendor with explicit SLA protections and a 90-day performance gate—balances the cost mandate against delivery risk. This is not a full switch until performance is verified. The 14-day deadline forces this now-or-defer decision; deferring past expiry moves to month-to-month and leaves the cost target unmet.
